title: Locality Administrator
company: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
description: Open only to applicants from Hampshire & Isle of Wight NHS system, which is limited to; Hampshire IOW Healthcare NHS Trust, Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB, Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust, Isle of Wight NHS Trust, University Hospital Southampton Foundation Trust, South Central Ambulance Service or Hampshire Hospitals Foundation Trust. An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic, committed and well-motivated Locality Administrator to join the Community Nursing and CIS Team based at Thomas Lewis House in Southampton. The Locality Administrator role is a pivotal part of the Service, supporting both the administrative and clinical teams across Southampton City. You will need to possess strong prioritising and excellent organisational skills together with the ability to remain calm in a busy and dynamic environment. The work is varied, challenging and fast paced which requires a flexible approach. We are looking for someone that has experience in working in a team. You need to be able to demonstrate strong communication skills, be organised and possess good IT skills, including competence with Microsoft Office. Experience of System One is desirable although all training will be provided. The successful applicant must be flexible, should possess excellent time management skills, be self-motivated and have a positive attitude with a customer focused approach. The role is full time based on 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday. Our core hours are 08:30 to 16:30. To provide comprehensive administrative support to the service. To work as part of a skill mix team to provide a comprehensive administrative support service. To effectively prioritise and manage own workload and oversee workload of team as necessary, whilst maintaining confidentiality and diplomacy at all times, both independently and as part of a team. To work without direct supervision and show extensive use of initiative in prioritising and making decisions in relation to effectively supporting the smooth operation of the service. To carry out other duties as necessary to meet the changing needs of HIOW Healthcare NHS Trust, accordance with management requirements and appropriate to banding. All duties will be carried out within the Trusts Information Governance, recording, and data sharing procedures and guidance. Further information about the Trust and this role can be found on the Job Description and Person Specification document attached. It is important to us that we ensure our recruitment processes are accessible and inclusive to everyone - if as a potential candidate you are concerned a person specification may prevent or restrict your application for employment as a result of unintentional barriers on the grounds of your sex, race, age, sexual orientation, religion/belief or disability please initially contact the Trust's Recruitment team - detailed in the advert. title: Administrator
company: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
description: Make a Difference Every Day Are you an organised, proactive administrator looking for a rewarding role where your work truly matters? We are recruiting for a 30hr - 37.5hr per week Administrator to join our friendly and supportive Central Community Mental Health Team (CMHT) based at College Keep. Our service provides specialist secondary mental health care for adults aged 18-65 living with severe and enduring mental health conditions. As a key member of our established administration team, you will play a vital role in supporting clinicians, consultants, service users and carers, helping to ensure the smooth running of a busy and compassionate service. At Central CMHT, we are committed to creating an inclusive, supportive workplace where staff wellbeing is a priority. You'll be joining a welcoming team environment that values collaboration, development and continuous learning. This is an opportunity to build a rewarding career while making a genuine difference to the lives of people accessing mental health services. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy helping people, and can remain calm and organised when managing competing priorities, we'd love to hear from you. What You'll Be Doing: As the first point of contact for many of our service users, you'll provide a professional, welcoming and supportive service while delivering essential administrative support to the wider clinical team. Key responsibilities include: Acting as the first point of contact for service users, carers and professionals Managing high volumes of telephone calls and enquiries Monitoring and responding to incoming emails Carrying out reception duties when required Processing referrals accurately and efficiently Booking and amending appointments Preparing and typing clinical correspondence Preparing agendas and taking meeting minutes Maintaining accurate records on our electronic patient record system (RIO) Providing administrative support to clinicians and the wider multidisciplinary team We're looking for someone who is: Enthusiastic, motivated and highly organised Able to work effectively in a busy environment with changing priorities A strong team player with a positive, can-do attitude Professional, compassionate and able to communicate confidently with a wide range of people Comfortable handling sensitive and confidential information Detail-focused with excellent administration skills Confident using Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and Outlook - training will be provided for our electronic patient record system, RIO. Able to maintain accurate records and demonstrate good literacy and numeracy skills Further information about the Trust and this role can be found on the Job Description and Person Specification document attached. description: Are you an organised, adaptable, and proactive individual who enjoys variety in your work. We are looking for a Flexible Business Support Administrator to join our Physical Health Service, providing essential support across multiple teams. No two days are the same in this role. While you will provide reception cover when required, your primary focus will be supporting three different teams across the service, stepping in where demand is greatest and ensuring our patients and staff continue to receive an excellent service. This is a unique opportunity to develop a broad understanding of physical health services, build relationships with a wide range of professionals. The role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast paced environment, enjoys learning new skills, and takes pride in making a real difference. Key Responsibilities Provide a welcoming and professional reception service when required. Offer administrative support across multiple physical health teams. Adapt quickly to changing priorities and service needs. Manage appointments, referrals, correspondence, and patient records. Support teams during periods of annual leave, sickness absence, and increased demand. Build effective working relationships with colleagues across the service. Help ensure smooth day-to-day operations and excellent patient experience. This role is for 34 hours per week. For further information about the post or for an informal discussion please call Jane Brown, Business Support Manager on 0300 123 6661.
